p1.title: Same-lock replacement swap is not specified to be atomic against a mid-flight deactivation of the current owner
p1.evidence: In packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts:194-230 the entry is read at :194, then two awaits (lock at :200, consumeCreatorSuccessorLive at :203, which internally runs activateV3LivePlane and only afterwards material.terminalizeSource at packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7371-7390) precede the map write at :229. The plan's token rule ('deletes the map entry and releases the stable-topic lock only if its token is still current') covers only post-swap stale cleanup. Before the swap the current token is still valid, so a concurrent deactivate of the existing wrapper passes the token check, deletes the entry, and releases the `ts-drp:${topic}` Web Lock (creator-adoption-activate.ts:143). This race is reachable from the product today: examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:1920-1963 shutdown() runs outside the lifetime-transition queue (enqueueLifetimeTransition at :2322-2330 serializes adoption only) and calls activeHandle.deactivate() mid-adoption. The in-flight replacement then re-installs an owner at :229 holding no browser lock, silently breaking the cross-tab single-writer guarantee the lock exists for; the plan names 'close/shutdown races' as a GREEN fault case but gives no rule that makes it pass.
p1.required_fix: Amend Batch 1 to state that the replacement re-validates the map entry and ownership token (compare-and-swap) after the last await and immediately before activeOwners.set; on mismatch the newly activated plane is torn down and the request fails closed, and a deactivation arriving during an in-flight replacement is either deferred until the swap settles or forces the replacement to fail. The failed-replacement retention guarantee should also state it preserves lock/identity custody, not old-plane usability, since terminalizeSource runs after the transport-reuse swap (v3-live.ts:7383-7390) and a post-reuse failure leaves the old registration already retired (v3-live.ts:7255-7260) with retry only via the existing pending-recovery/reopen path.

p1.title: The plan's pinned audit evidence is absent from the signed checkpoint commit
p1.evidence: The plan (docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md, D.110c-b section) pins .logs/d110c-b-plan-audit-3118da76/audit.md and source-shape.txt with SHA-256 61d34473…/49bb0fc6… plus a 'validating self-excluding manifest SHA-256' 1ea2c137…, but commit aa002e78 contains exactly one file (+218 lines, the plan markdown only) and `git ls-tree -r HEAD` shows no .logs/d110c-b-* path, while every prior slice's review/audit ledger under .logs/ is committed (e.g. .logs/d110c-0b0-confirmation-43290dab). The pinned hashes are therefore unverifiable by any reviewer, violating the plan's own changed-path/hash/manifest custody discipline at the checkpoint that anchors the whole slice. The audit's technical claims themselves check out against source (creator-adoption.ts:373/545/565/610/666, creator-adoption-commit.ts:434/491, creator-adoption-activate.ts:52-57/189-230, examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:235-242/453-488/2265-2287/3500-3586 all confirmed), so this is an evidence-custody defect, not an audit-correctness one.
p1.required_fix: Commit the referenced audit ledger, source-shape record, and self-excluding manifest under .logs/d110c-b-plan-audit-3118da76/ with hashes matching the plan's pins (or amend the plan to drop the unverifiable pins) before any RED begins.

p2.title: Compatibility boundary omits the epoch-pinned authority guard in the product contract fixture
p2.evidence: tests/fixtures/phase-6a-v3/creator-successor-product-contract.ts:560-580 exports isD108d2Authority, documented as 'the exact epoch-one creator projection', which hard-requires record.epoch === 1; tests/phase-6a-creator-successor-product-red.test.ts:79-82 pins its epoch rejection. After widening V3RoomSuccessorAuthority.epoch (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:237) to a validated positive number, a genuine epoch-2 authority fails this guard, so the new Batch 2 Chromium test cannot validate its epoch-2 authority through the existing contract without generalizing it. The plan names only the phase-5e declaration as a tests-only widening.
p2.disposition: Amend the boundary paragraph to enumerate isD108d2Authority/D108D2_AUTHORITY_KEYS and its red test as tests-only generalizations (positive safe integer; epoch 0 must remain rejected). No public change; caught anyway by the mandatory changed-path/source-shape gates.

p2.title: The phase-5e 'CreatorLiveCloseResult declaration' reference is misnamed
p2.evidence: No identifier named CreatorLiveCloseResult exists in packages/storage-browser/tests/phase-5e-creator-live-close.pw.ts; the literal-pinned pair epoch: 0 / successorEpoch: 1 lives in the inline anonymous sealEpoch() return type at lines 249-262 (the production CreatorLiveCloseResult in packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:65-77 already ships number fields from D.110c-a).
p2.disposition: Correct the reference to the inline sealEpoch declaration when the plan text is next amended; the intended widening is unambiguous and needs no re-review.

p2.title: Batch 1's Node GREEN lists a 'one browser lock' proof that is vacuous in the Node runner
p2.evidence: The root Vitest project (vite.config.mts:87-112) uses the default node environment with no window/navigator.locks, so browserLockRealm() (creator-adoption-activate.ts:106-114) is false and acquireBrowserLock returns undefined — no lock exists to count in the Node test; the genuine lock proof exists only in the Batch 2 Chromium gate, which already lists 'exactly one active owner/lock'.
p2.disposition: Reword the Batch 1 gate as map-custody-only (one active topic owner) and leave the exact lock proof to the Chromium gate; no design change.

summary: The plan's diagnosis is accurate and its core design is sound: RED is genuinely causal (the frozen chain-invalid is exactly the creator-adoption.ts:371-374 gen-1-only projection filter rejecting the genuine D.110c-a epoch-1 close, and the browser RED rides the real stale close handle whose close() rejects once lifecycle is successor-adopted, creator-close.ts:468-475); epoch/kind derivation from authenticated trust is sufficient because openCreatorSuccessorTrust already enforces successor == current+1 (protocol-v3/creator-close.ts:615-619), and 0->1 stays byte-identical; v3-live.ts:1928 already implements the epoch-general kind rule so no new authority is needed; store reuse across epochs is feasible since seal vote/evidence rows are epoch-keyed (seal-vote-store.ts:164/281, seal-evidence.ts:50-74, packages/seal/src/creator.ts:438-447); GREEN gates honestly prove 0->1->2 plus a genuine 2->3 close without cold-reopen or long-horizon claims, and no silent public/wire/dependency widening is required beyond the declared epoch-field change. Two blockers remain: the same-lock replacement design lacks swap-atomicity against a mid-flight deactivation/shutdown that can release the browser lock under an in-flight replacement, and the signed plan commit omits the very audit-ledger evidence it pins by hash. Both are correctable without changing the design's shape.
